title: Gemini 4 Neon looks like an Opus 5.5 competitor
lede: A post from the Agent Duel team projects that Gemini 4 Neon would land just behind Claude Opus 5.5 on its coding-agent leaderboard, by assuming Carbon's quality at Neon's much higher speed.

points: Gemini 4 Carbon tops the Agent Duel leaderboard when early votes are excluded, but runs at only about 46 tokens per second.
On launch day, OpenRouter served Neon at about 127 tokens per second.
The author modeled win rate from model identity, speed and early voting, and found speed roughly as important as the model itself.
The projection gives Neon an Elo of 1,066 against 1,078 for Opus 5.5, a 90% interval of -94 to +68, and a 48.3% expected win rate.

points.text: Readers object to projecting the score of a model that is already out; the author concedes and frames the post as a study of speed.
Commenters say models now specialise, one running Fable as orchestrator with Opus workers and doubting Gemini on long sessions.
Harness choice is contested: one commenter finds Copilot weaker than Claude Code on the same model, while the author's data says it matters less.
Early users are impressed, with one calling Neon the first Google model that feels good for coding, though speed doubts linger.
Cost comes up as well, and the author notes DeepSeek wins about half its duels by being very fast and good enough.
